title: Effect of Al Content on Inclusions in Fe-15Mn- Al-C Low-Density Steel
abstract: Three experiments of Fe-15Mn- Al-C ( = 1, 3, 5) low-density steel with different Al contents are carried out, and the characteristics of inclusions are observed through field-emission scanning electron microscopy. The results show that the types of inclusions in the three samples are almost the same, mainly $\mathsf { A l } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O } _ { 3 } , \mathsf { A l N } ,$ MnS, TiN, ${ \sf A l } _ { 2 } { \sf O } _ { 3 }$ -MnS, AlN-MnS, TiN-MnS, and $\mathsf { A l } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O } _ { 3 } { \cdot } \mathsf { A l N } { \cdot } \mathsf { M n S } .$ The number percentage of ${ \sf A l } _ { 2 } { \sf O } _ { 3 }$ decreases, while the number percentage of AlN increases with the increase of Al content in the three samples. As the Al content increases, the number of inclusions between 1 and 5 μm decreases, while the number between 5 and 10 μm increases. FactSage8.2 software calculation shows that an increase in Al content leads to an increase in the liquidus and a decrease in the solidus of the steel; at the same time, it causes the austenite region to narrow and expands the ferrite region. The change in the solidification route leads to a delay in the solidification fraction of AlN, MnS, and TiN inclusions precipitation. At last, the 2D mismatch theory shows that the mismatch degrees of $\mathbf { \Delta A l _ { 2 } O _ { 3 } } / \mathbf { M n S } ,$ AlN/MnS, TiN/MnS, and $\mathsf { A l N } / \mathsf { A l } _ { 2 } \mathsf { O } _ { 3 }$ are 8.41%, 8.94%, 11.65%, and 11.66%, respectively.
